overrides.reason: The strict-pre-vote HF3682 second engrossment adds a grantee fraud-risk rating system and corresponding grants-management procedures for all executive agencies in amended Minn. Stat. 16B.97, subd.4, and appropriates $71,000 for Office of Grants Management templates/training. This is an actual, proposed state-program fraud-risk prevention and accountability mechanism directly within Robbins's broader state oversight/transparency stance.

The exact pre-vote SF856 tenth engrossment creates independent Office of the Inspector General under proposed chapter 15D, empowered to investigate fraud/misuse across state agencies, stop/freeze public funds when appropriate, make referrals, receive fraud reports and publish systemic accountability reports. It concretely strengthens fraud oversight and transparency for state-funded programs, directly matching Robbins's broad pre-vote public-fund accountability stance.

HF3298 would reimburse replacement of obsolete single-walled underground petroleum storage piping out of the petroleum tank fund; reducing petroleum release risks is plausibly environmental protection. Harder's exact frozen claim, however, ties environmental protection to *strengthening conservation programs*, while this measure is commercial petroleum storage modernization/compensation, not a demonstrated conservation program. Do not infer full claim applicability from a generalized ecological benefit.

SF856 provides real cross-agency anti-fraud investigation and prevention tools plus new agency duties to publicize fraud-reporting tools and cooperate with Inspector General requests, including producing reports demanded in investigations. Yet those provisions do not independently establish the ongoing stricter obligation for *state agencies to report fraud incidents* that Rarick's joined state-agency fraud-reporting-and-prevention source proposition specifies. Agency web links and inspector-general reports cannot silently substitute for agency incident reporting.

The exact SF4612 third engrossment increases FY2027 DHS Office of Inspector General central-office funds by $26,000 yet separately reduces grants for fraud prevention by $425,000 in the same human-services appropriations article. Because the mixed positive and negative changes to oversight/fraud-prevention resources have no proven net fraud-control direction, Robbins's broad stronger-oversight proposition cannot safely receive an alignment or conflict label from this omnibus.

SF4476's third engrossment newly appropriates $1,284,000 in FY2027 and raises future baseline funding for the DHS central-office Inspector General, but the frozen section lacks new specified fraud-detection/reporting powers or explicit anti-fraud use for the allocation. Other provider fraud-withholding and complaint provisions occur in existing carried-forward law. Increased office resources alone cannot establish Robbins's broader substantive fraud-oversight direction without an independently pinned use-of-funds link.

SF4612's proposed 142H.13 behavior-guidance statutory text forbids physical punishment, rough handling, shaking, restraints and humiliation in child-care centers, precisely the childcare/young-child actor and abuse context of Scott's source. However pre-vote Minnesota Rule 9503.0055 already prohibited many of these acts and required behavior-guidance policies; the omnibus appears to modernize and recodify substantial existing regulation. Without demonstrating that the exact changes *strengthen* infant/young-child abuse safeguards beyond existing rules, the direction and applicability must fail closed.
